content:
We have already heard several rumors about Apple's next-generation iPad mini, including the adoption of an OLED display and improved waterproof design.

A new leak today indicates that the upcoming iPad mini will feature powerful performance: an all-new A20 Pro chip.

MacRumors today discovered information related to the new iPad mini in Apple's code, including an icon purportedly representing the device.

The icon shows that the overall design of the new iPad mini will remain the same as the current model. However, the camera has been moved from the top bezel to the landscape side, aligning with the layout of Apple's other iPad models. A small speaker opening has also been added at the top of the display, in a design similar to the iPhone.

The code also shows that the new iPad mini will feature the A20 Pro chip, the same as the chip used in the iPhone 18 Pro series launched last week. The currently available iPad mini was released in October 2024, featuring the Apple A17 Pro chip.

According to Mark Gurman, the new iPad mini is expected to go on sale before the end of October. In addition to the changes mentioned above, the new iPad mini is reported to offer improved waterproofing and a brand-new speaker system.

For more details, you can read our complete preview roundup of the new iPad mini.

A separate independent report today also revealed the specifications of the next-generation basic iPad, including the A19 chip, 8GB of memory, and Apple's self-developed N1 and C1X connectivity chips.
